import unittest
from settings import effective_limit

class TestEffectiveLimit(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_none_means_default(self):
        # None means default (default is 10 in settings.py)
        self.assertEqual(effective_limit(None), 10)

    def test_zero_means_zero(self):
        # Zero means disabled and must stay zero
        self.assertEqual(effective_limit(0), 0)

    def test_positive_int_overrides(self):
        # Positive int overrides default
        self.assertEqual(effective_limit(5), 5)
        self.assertEqual(effective_limit(100), 100)

    def test_negative_int_raises_value_error(self):
        # Negative int raises ValueError
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "Limit cannot be negative"):
            effective_limit(-1)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "Limit cannot be negative"):
            effective_limit(-50)

        self.assertEqual(effective_limit(), 10)
